scope: Shared temporary DDL resolution, DROP split and completion, preprocessor/grant admission, transaction and observation lifecycle, shared global table-ID allocation and TRUNCATE replacement; existing-owner maintenance.
repairs: Temporary DDL now resolves the same local overlay for grants and execution: ordinary/mixed DROP skips local privileges, while local ALTER/index/rename reaches its own refusal instead of the hidden permanent object. GLOBAL DROP kind errors precede grants/commit; explicit local mismatch notes remain combined. Complete planner visit ownership remains open.

Local CREATE/LIKE and TRUNCATE now reserve real global metadata IDs through an independent transaction; TRUNCATE replaces local storage and memory auto-ID allocators. This fixes collisions with persistent objects. Ordinary and mixed DROP now split local names before cluster lowering, preserve original visits, and retire local targets only after persistent success. Local-only DROP and explicit local mismatches preserve the transaction; ordinary local ALTER/index/rename refusals occur after Go's implicit commit and cannot mutate hidden persistent metadata. The direct metadata transaction still lacks complete durable DDL job ownership. Its existing multi-persistent DROP planner also rejects missing names before applying present targets, unlike Go’s per-object job loop; that residual is not repaired by local-target splitting.

Local ALTER (including grouped actions), CREATE/DROP INDEX and RENAME now use the session overlay refusal owner; the cluster path cannot mutate the permanent table hidden by a local target. Shared DROP resolution and implicit-commit policy preserve local/persistent lifetimes. Complete durable multi-schema ownership remains unresolved.

Mixed DROP keeps original local/persistent table visits in one routed observation; local completion no longer reparses or starts a second SQL statement. Broader plan/runtime metadata and complete package obligations remain unresolved.
removals: Unconditional CREATE-only DDL commit rule in both session wrappers
DROP reparsing in Session and wrapper parsing for local DDL
